summary_paragraph: A 68-year-old female with chronic diastolic heart failure, end-stage renal disease, and atrial fibrillation was admitted following an episode of chest pain and severe hypotension during hemodialysis. The chest pain resolved with dialysis, and cardiac biomarkers showed no evidence of acute myocardial infarction. She was monitored on telemetry with no recurrent symptoms. An echocardiogram confirmed preserved ejection fraction with outflow tract obstruction. Electrophysiology recommended increasing amiodarone to 600 mg daily for one week, then 400 mg daily, and warfarin was adjusted to 2 mg daily. She underwent uneventful hemodialysis on hospital day two and remained hemodynamically stable. Her left eye symptoms improved with continuation of home ophthalmic medications. She was discharged home in good condition with updated medication instructions, emphasis on fluid and sodium restriction, daily weight monitoring, and close follow-up with cardiology and nephrology.
